_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 12. Blau notes consulted: 12:1 (אד' קאל — 'when he said'; Cairo follows Derenbourg/Tag/Kapach reading; Blau prefers Petersburg 'תם קאל'); 12:20 (ד'רקובה = 'escorted him' — classical Arabic בדרק, per Blau 12:20). Saadia-specific: שכם=Nablus (12:6), הנגבה=אלקבלה ('the qibla / the southern direction', 12:9), v.7 תגלי' = 'appeared' (anti-anthropomorphic — God 'caused himself to be revealed', not literal visual appearance), v.17 פתואעד = 'threatened' (rationalizes וינגע = 'struck'). Cairo prints 'אברהם' (long form) in v.1 but 'אברם' (short form) elsewhere; rendering 'Abram' throughout until Gen 17 renaming.

translations.1: When God said to Abram: 'Go forth from your land and your birthplace and the house of your father, to the land which I shall show you;
translations.2: and I shall make of you a great nation, and bless you, and magnify your name; and you shall be a blessing.
translations.3: And I shall bless those who bless you, and curse those who revile you; and in you shall be blessed all the clans of the earth.'
translations.4: And Abram went forth, as God had said to him; and Lot went with him. And Abram was a son of seventy-five years when he went out from Haran.
translations.5: And Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother's son, and all their possessions which they had acquired, and the souls which they had acquired in Haran; and they went forth to go to the land of Canaan, and they came to it.
translations.6: And Abram traveled about in the land, as far as the place of Nablus (Shechem), as far as the plain of Moreh. And the Canaanites were in it at that time.
translations.7: Then God appeared to him, and said: 'To your offspring shall I give this land.' And he built there an altar to the God who had appeared to him.
translations.8: And he moved from there to the mountain east of Beth-El; and he pitched his tent there — with Beth-El to the west, and the Ai to the east — and he built there an altar to God, and called upon His name.
translations.9: And Abram journeyed onward — each time time passed, he journeyed onward — toward the qibla (the south).
translations.10: Then there was a famine in the land; and Abram went down to Egypt to sojourn there, since the famine was severe in the land.
translations.11: And when he drew near to entering Egypt, he said to Sarai his wife: 'Behold, I know that you are beautiful in appearance.
translations.12: I fear that, if the Egyptians see you, they will say, "This is his wife"; and they will kill me and keep you alive.
translations.13: Say that you are my sister, so that it may go well with me on your account, and my soul may live because of you.'
translations.14: And when Abram entered Egypt, the Egyptians saw the woman — that she was very beautiful.
translations.15: And the officials of Pharaoh saw her, and they praised her to him; and the woman was taken to his house.
translations.16: And he treated Abram well on her account; and he had sheep, and cattle, and donkeys, and male and female slaves, and she-asses, and camels.
translations.17: And God threatened Pharaoh with great plagues, and his household, on account of Sarai, the wife of Abram.
translations.18: And Pharaoh summoned Abram, and said to him: 'What is this that you have done to me? Why did you not tell me that she is your wife?
translations.19: Why did you say, "She is my sister," so that I took her for myself as a wife? And now — behold, your wife: take her and go.'
translations.20: And Pharaoh appointed men over him; and they escorted him out, and his wife, and all that he had.
